statements.quote: The two tasks used (listing uses for a paperclip and generating ideas to return employees to the workplace) are adaptations of the AUT that align with real-world entrepreneurial and managerial challenges.
statements.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1437), Methodology, third paragraph; task-material description, not an availability statement.

statements.quote: All participants received identical verbal and written instructions prior to task commencement including watching a 2-minute instructional video on how to prompt ChatGPT-3.5, but otherwise developed their own prompts according to their understanding. The task was administered by a researcher who was not the classroom teacher. Responses were submitted to the Learning Management System (LMS) via a non-graded item on the LMS that repeated the same instructions delivered by the researcher in-class and provided a submission site.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1438), Measures and procedures, second paragraph; instructional materials and internal submission site, with no public link.

statements.quote: To further strengthen the reliability and validity of the assessment, the three raters used a rubric with definitions for each indicator, adapted from widely accepted creativity literature that captures diverse aspects of divergent thinking as a measure of potential for creative thinking (Runco and Acar 2012; Said-Metwaly, Noortgate, and Kyndt 2017). Prior to rating, the raters met online to review and discuss the marking rubric used to assess flexibility, originality and elaboration. This step ensured a shared understanding of the criteria, which were rated on a 5-point scale from Exceptional to Insufficient. Each rater independently scored the same submission and discussed their reasoning to align interpretations. This process was repeated six times, moderating 12 submissions (six for the paperclip task and six for the return-to-office task), resulting in a consensus on how to apply the rubric categories.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1438), Measures and procedures, third paragraph; scoring rubric description, with no deposited rubric or code identified.

statements.quote: Student submissions to the LMS were downloaded into a spreadsheet, with incomplete data and submissions from students who did not consent to participate in the research removed from the sample. The refined datasets were then distributed to each rater, who iteratively reviewed all responses. Raters recorded the fluency count and used the rubric to evaluate flexibility, originality and elaboration. Each rater assessed the submissions from all participating students.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1438), Measures and procedures, paragraph immediately after measures (1)-(4); internal data handling, not public sharing.

statements.quote: The terms on which this article has been published allow the posting of the Accepted Manuscript in a repository by the author(s) or with their consent.
statements.locator: PDF p. 2 (journal p. 1432), copyright/open-access footnote; permission to post the accepted manuscript, not participant data.

notes: Checked on 2026-10-09. Read the complete 66,786-character markdown conversion, including the note, acknowledgements, disclosure, and references; the saved PDF has 16 pages including the publisher cover, and contains no appendix. Checked PDF hyperlink annotations and extracted PDF pp. 8, 12, and 13 with PyMuPDF. No data-availability or code-availability statement, request-only offer, preregistration, supplementary-file notice, or repository link for the trial appears in the saved article. The quotations in statements are descriptions of study data/materials and a manuscript-posting permission; none promises public access to the participant records. The screening form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty. There were therefore no named data/code deposits whose file inventories could be requested. Bibliographic reference links and author profiles were not treated as trial deposits. Publisher checks: GET https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2025.2515512 with Accept including application/json returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://api.crossref.org/v1/works/10.1080%2F03075079.2025.2515512/transform (metadata, not a supplement listing). GET https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03075079.2025.2515512 returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot check. Stopped at that barrier; the publisher landing page and possible supplementary files could not be inspected. No login, access request, or bot-check bypass was attempted. All API requests used User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 without an email address or authentication. No relevant deposit was found in the four requested sources or the additional Figshare searches. No participant-data file was available for column or row inspection. For S1 and S2, public data therefore do not currently resolve final.open_items on analyzed counts by arm/discipline, distinct-person assignment/attrition, unlabeled dispersion statistics, the MANOVA reporting discrepancies, rater aggregation/scale coding, randomization procedures, or allocation of outlier exclusions. Per-person means, SDs, SEs and diversity measures from submitted ideas cannot be computed from a confirmed public dataset. Medium confidence reflects the blocked publisher check and the limits of repository indexing; none_found means no deposit was identified, not proof that no deposit exists.
